findings.summary: Date.parse read a zone-less date-time as local time, so clones in different timezones ordered the same brain differently (materialize winner, pin, retire). Fixed in 9b57f38: ISO-only timestampMs, zone-less read as UTC; TZ child-process test.
Comparator is not a total order when parseable and unparseable values mix (cycle a<b<x<a). After the ISO gate it needs a non-ISO value; lexical fallback kept so 'unknown' still sorts above ISO.
Date.parse accepted non-dates ('1', 'hello 2026'). Fixed by the ISO gate in 9b57f38.
export.ts departures sort left lexical. Fixed in 9b57f38.
Day-level checks slice the raw string (engine.ts valid_until gate, export asOfDate). Out of #374 scope; filed as #474.
10 of 16 converted sites have no #374 test.

main's Tier-1 curation createdMs used Date.parse, so archiving was host-timezone dependent and disagreed with the comparator (Tokyo archived N3, UTC/LA archived E). Fixed in 36a7a66 after merging main; three-TZ autoCurate test.
pin-staleness.ts Date.parse(pin.created) gives a zone-less pin a host-timezone cutoff (matches git --before). Carried to #474.
No test for lowercase t/z (removing the /i flag survives).
Rolling dates such as 2026-02-30 are accepted (V8 leniency), deterministically across hosts.
The new curation TZ test leaves a vfkb-tz-* temp dir per run.

Values Date.parse accepted but the ISO gate rejects (+05, 'Oct 22 2026', :60) now read as NaN in curation: such a candidate is skipped, such a pin skips the run. Safe direction, consistent with the comparator.

the local user-prompt-submit failure passes alone (#470)
vilosource identity and no AI attribution on all branch commits
